meta.about: A context cell that can be raised says how far, and the maximum is called "max" on every row, so no cell's ceiling is left to the model's imagination.
meta.recorded-outcome: asked "Which runtime has highest potential context?", Gemma answered "The WebLLM has the highest potential context, with a context size of 1–4K raisable." The cell said "1–4K raisable" with no ceiling, beside wllama's stated 256K, and a literal reader has nothing to rule WebLLM out with. With the ceiling added, the same one-step question still picked WebLLM, now by matching "max" to "raisable to a max of"; asked to rank the rows first, it ranked them correctly. That remainder is the 2B model. A system-prompt line asking it to list values before comparing fixed two questions and broke a third, so it was not kept.
meta.guards: the `value` on the raisable Context cells in index.html, and the `raisable` words in `MATRIX_NOTES` in deck/components.js. Drop either and the `re:` line finds no ceiling. The reply is kept verbatim as the input that exposed it; the assertion is on what the model was told.
